userStories.title: ContextBuilderService — Shared Retrieval Contract
acceptanceCriteria: getProjectContext(query) returns all four top-level blocks: canonicalState, retrievedContext, provenance, and meta
canonicalState.recentEvents is ordered by createdAt DESC and limited to 20 events
retrievedContext.semanticMemory is ordered by confidence DESC and limited to 10 items
retrievedContext.documents calls HybridRetrieverService.search() internally
When query is blank or absent, retrievedContext.documents.results is an empty array and HybridRetrieverService.search() is not called
When intent='plan', getProjectContext excludes canonicalState.recentEvents from the response

tokenBudget truncation removes lower-priority blocks first (codeIntel before graphPaths before documents before semanticMemory) and never removes canonicalState.tickets or canonicalState.activeDecisions; when intent='plan', canonicalState.recentEvents is always excluded unconditionally (not as a budget-truncation step)
meta.latencyMs measures wall-clock time from entry to return (excluding network)
When getProjectContext is called with a non-existent projectId, it throws ProjectNotFoundError with code='PROJECT_NOT_FOUND'
All errors thrown by getProjectContext are KodaError subclasses and serialize to the ErrorEnvelope format

The context controller route is gated with @RequiredPermission([KodaAction.READ, 'ProjectContext']) and additionally enforces project membership via a checkProjectMembership() inline call (following the existing pattern in ProjectsController — no ProjectMembershipGuard class exists; do not create one); the controller uses @Principal() principal: KodaPrincipal with no inline actorType or role checks
Repeated calls with identical input and unchanged underlying data produce the same result ordering across all agent adapters
suggestedCriteria: When includeGraph=false (default), retrievedContext.graphPaths is undefined in the response
When includeCodeIntel=false (default), retrievedContext.codeIntel is undefined in the response
When repoRefs is a non-empty array, includeCodeIntel defaults to true
When tokenBudget is not provided, getProjectContext applies a default budget of 4000 tokens
KodaCaslAbilityFactory grants READ ProjectContext to: ADMIN users, all agent principals (any role), and user principals with projectRole DEVELOPER or VIEWER
When a user principal without project membership calls the context route, the response is 403 Forbidden

userStories.title: Policy Gates — Isolation, Provenance, Write Safety, GraphifyEnabled, TokenBudget
acceptanceCriteria: IsolationGate runs 10 queries that should return 0 results for project-A and asserts all 10 return 0 results
IsolationGate seeds project-A and project-B, then queries project-B-specific terms while scoped to project-A, and asserts no project-B data is returned
ProvenanceGate runs 20 fixture search queries with known matching results and asserts every non-empty response has provenance.sources.length > 0

WriteGate runs KodaDomainWriter writes and asserts they succeed; direct raw Prisma writes (PrismaService.client.*) outside approved layers in CI test mode throw a KodaError with code='WRITE_GATE_VIOLATION'

TruthConsistencyGate picks 10 random canonical ticket IDs, queries both CanonicalStateService.getSnapshot() and raw Prisma ticket rows (prisma.client.ticket.findMany), and asserts that status, priority, and title match for each ticket (any field mismatch counts as a discrepancy); this is the definition of 'derived store' in this gate
GraphifyEnabledGate runs 10 queries on a project with graphifyEnabled=false and asserts zero results have source='code'
TokenBudgetGate calls getProjectContext with tokenBudget=1000, measures meta.tokensUsed, and asserts tokensUsed <= 1050
All gates are runnable via bun run policy:gates -- --project=X
When any gate fails, PolicyGateResult.blockedReason is non-null and describes the failure
Gate results are written to apps/api/test/policy-gates/results.json for CI artifact capture
Policy gates set up deterministic fixture data and do not read production, staging, or developer-local projects
suggestedCriteria: When IsolationGate detects a cross-project data leak, it records a leakageIncident via SloDashboardService.recordQueryMetric() (once US-004 is wired)
When bun run policy:gates is run without the --project flag, the runner exits with code 1 and prints a usage error to stderr
When all six gates pass, PolicyGateResult.passed is true and blockedReason is undefined
When PolicyGateService.runAllGates() encounters an unexpected exception in a single gate, that gate's GateResult.error is set and the remaining gates still run

userStories.title: Agent Adapter Registry
acceptanceCriteria: AgentRegistryService.register() stores the adapter and it is retrievable by agentId via getAdapter()
AgentRegistryService.getAdapter('claude-code') returns an adapter with formatContext() that formats GetProjectContextResponse as a Claude Code prompt fragment
AgentRegistryService.getAdapter('nax') returns an adapter with formatContext() that formats GetProjectContextResponse for nax prompt injection
Calling register() twice with the same agentId replaces the existing adapter
KodaAgentAdapter.getContextForAgent(agentId, query) calls ContextBuilderService.getProjectContext() and then registry.getAdapter(agentId).formatContext()
The registry is seeded with adapters for claude-code and nax on app startup (onModuleInit or equivalent)
Adapters cannot call retrieval, memory, graph, or code-intel services directly; they only receive the already-built GetProjectContextResponse
suggestedCriteria: When AgentRegistryService.getAdapter() is called with an unregistered agentId, it throws an error with a descriptive message identifying the missing agentId
AgentRegistryService.listAgents() returns a list containing at least the claude-code and nax entries seeded at startup
When formatContext() is called on the nax adapter, the returned string contains the projectId and intent from response.meta
When formatContext() is called on the claude-code adapter, the returned string contains a structured prompt fragment with canonicalState and retrievedContext sections

userStories.title: SLO Dashboard + Token Budget Metrics
acceptanceCriteria: recordQueryMetric() persists a MemoryQueryMetric record with fields: projectId, latencyMs, intent, tokensUsed, hadProvenance, staleHitCount, resultCount, and createdAt
getSloMetrics({ from, to }) computes p50, p95, and p99 latency percentiles from persisted latencyMs records in the time window
staleHitRate is computed as sum(staleHitCount) / sum(resultCount) in the time window, returning 0 when sum(resultCount) is 0
provenanceCoverage is computed as count(hadProvenance=true) / count(total queries in window)
Stale hit counts are recorded when HybridRetrieverService.search() returns results whose indexedAt is more than 7 days old
leakageIncidents is computed as sum(leakageIncidentCount) over all records in the time window
GET /admin/slos?from=X&to=Y returns the full SloMetrics object as JSON
Metrics persist enough fields to compute all SloMetrics fields without reading raw context response bodies
suggestedCriteria: When getSloMetrics is called with a time window that has no records, retrievalLatency.sampleCount is 0 and all percentile values are 0
When ContextBuilderService.getProjectContext() completes, it calls recordQueryMetric() as fire-and-forget; an error in recordQueryMetric() does not propagate to the caller

GET /admin/slos is gated with @RequiredPermission([KodaAction.READ, 'AdminScope']) and returns 403 for non-admin principals; KodaCaslAbilityFactory must be updated to grant READ AdminScope to ADMIN users (the current factory only grants MANAGE on ADMIN_MANAGEABLE_RESOURCES and does not include AdminScope — add { action: READ, subject: 'AdminScope' } to the ADMIN branch in userPermissions())
memoryGrowthRate is computed from MemoryItem.createdAt over the last 7 days, not from MemoryQueryMetric records

userStories.title: CI Pipeline Integration
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Wire policy gates and SLO metrics into the CI pipeline so every PR runs gates, fails on violations, and produces an artifact with gate results and SLO snapshot.

**Motivation** — Gates and metrics are only valuable if they block merges automatically; without CI wiring, they are opt-in and will be skipped.

**Approach** — Add the `policy:gates` script to `apps/api/package.json` that runs `PolicyGateService.runAllGates()` with a deterministic test project, prints a PASS/FAIL summary table to stdout, writes `apps/api/test/policy-gates/results.json`, and exits with code 1 when `PolicyGateResult.passed === false`. Add a CI step (GitHub Actions workflow or equivalent) that runs `bun run policy:gates -- --project=test-project` and uploads `results.json` as an artifact. Add a second CI step (or extend the same job) that exports the current SLO metrics snapshot to a JSON artifact after the gates run.

**Scope** — In: policy:gates npm script in apps/api/package.json, CI workflow step for gate execution, CI artifact upload for results.json and SLO snapshot. Out: blocking on SLO threshold violations in CI (informational artifact only), dashboard UI.
acceptanceCriteria: CI pipeline runs bun run policy:gates -- --project=test-project on every PR
CI pipeline fails with exit code 1 when PolicyGateResult.passed === false
bun run policy:gates outputs a summary table to stdout with PASS or FAIL per gate
SLO metrics are exported to a JSON artifact after each CI run

routing.noTestJustification: This story adds a CI workflow step and an npm script entry. The CI step has no runtime behavior beyond invoking the policy:gates command (tested in US-002) and uploading an artifact. No new application logic is introduced that a unit or integration test could cover.

suggestedCriteria: When bun run policy:gates exits with code 0, the results.json artifact contains a PolicyGateResult with passed=true and all gates listed
When bun run policy:gates exits with code 1, the CI step annotation includes the blockedReason from PolicyGateResult

analysis:
Phase 5 is an integration and hardening phase that composes Phase 1-4 services behind a single shared contract. Key findings from codebase exploration:

**Existing services (ready to consume):**
- `apps/api/src/memory/canonical-state.service.ts` — CanonicalStateService with CanonicalSnapshot, CanonicalTicket, CanonicalEvent, CanonicalDecision
- `apps/api/src/memory/timeline.service.ts` — TimelineService with getProjectTimeline() and getTicketHistory()
- `apps/api/src/memory/prisma-memory-item.repository.ts` — PrismaMemoryItemRepository (the 'MemoryService' the spec references)
- `apps/api/src/rag/hybrid-retriever.service.ts` — HybridRetrieverService with HybridSearchQuery/HybridSearchResult, intent-aware weighting
- `apps/api/src/entity-graph/entity-graph.service.ts` — EntityGraphService with EntityRecord, ImpactAnalysis
- `apps/api/src/code-intel/impact-analysis.service.ts` — ImpactAnalysisService with ChangeImpactQuery/ChangeImpactResult
- `apps/api/src/koda-domain-writer/koda-domain-writer.service.ts` — KodaDomainWriter (approved write layer)

**Existing ContextBuilderService (Phase 3 prototype):**
`apps/api/src/memory/context-builder.service.ts` exists but has a much simpler interface (no canonicalState, no retrievedContext, no provenance, no meta, no token budget). Phase 5 spec calls for the new canonical service at `apps/api/src/context/context-builder.service.ts`. The Phase 3 prototype should be replaced or delegated from. The implementing agent must create a new `ContextModule` and move/replace the builder there.

**Missing infrastructure (all new):**
- `apps/api/src/context/context-builder.service.ts` — the unified service (spec: create new)
- `apps/api/src/policy/policy-gate.service.ts` — no policy gate infrastructure exists
- `apps/api/src/agents/agent-registry.service.ts` — no registry exists (agents/ module has AgentsService for CRUD management but not an adapter registry)
- `apps/api/src/monitoring/slo-dashboard.service.ts` — no metrics collection exists
- `MemoryQueryMetric` Prisma model — does not exist; requires new migration

**CASL changes required:**
- `apps/api/src/auth/casl/koda-action.enum.ts` — `KodaSubject` type does not include `'ProjectContext'`; must add it
- `apps/api/src/auth/casl/koda-casl-ability.factory.ts` — must grant `READ ProjectContext` to: ADMIN users, agents (any role), and project members with DEVELOPER/VIEWER role

**Auth pattern reference:**
- Two-layer pattern: `@RequiredPermission([KodaAction.READ, 'ProjectContext'])` decorator handles role gate; `ProjectMembershipGuard` (or equivalent check from projects/ module) handles per-project membership until CASL project-scoped conditions land
- `@Principal() principal: KodaPrincipal` must be used in controllers — no inline actorType/role checks

**Module composition:**
- `apps/api/src/app.module.ts` needs new ContextModule, PolicyModule, MonitoringModule imports
- Each new service needs its own NestJS module

**Token estimation:**
- No existing tokenizer in the repo; use the deterministic approximation `ceil(characters / 4)` in a single shared helper

**Policy gates CI script:**
- `apps/api/package.json` needs a `policy:gates` script entry
- Gates must use a real (not mocked) database with deterministic test fixture data
- Results written to `apps/api/test/policy-gates/results.json`

**ResponseProvenance type:**
- The spec references `ResponseProvenance` — this type likely needs to be defined as part of US-001. The rag/ module has provenance concepts in code-intel; the implementing agent should check `apps/api/src/code-intel/impact-analysis.service.ts` for the existing `Provenance` interface and align or extend it.

**Prisma schema:**
- `MemoryQueryMetric` model needs to be added with fields: id, projectId, intent, latencyMs, tokensUsed (optional), hadProvenance, staleHitCount, resultCount, leakageIncidentCount, createdAt; with composite indexes on (projectId, createdAt) and (createdAt)
- `memoryGrowthRate` SLO metric is computed from existing `MemoryItem.createdAt`, not from MemoryQueryMetric

**Dependency build order:**
1. US-001 (ContextBuilderService) — foundation for all others
2. US-003 (AgentRegistryService) and US-004 (SLO Dashboard) — both depend on US-001, can parallelize
3. US-002 (Policy Gates) — depends on US-001 and the domain writer
4. US-005 (CI Integration) — depends on US-002 and US-004
